description: Spatial-vs-non-spatial R-Precision on the released MDM checkpoint, no training, full HumanML3D test split generated once.

fid_results.note: generated_vs_real_fid is NOT directly comparable across subsets of different size -- FID's estimator bias grows as n shrinks, so a smaller subset shows a higher FID for that reason alone, independent of model quality. real_vs_real_floor (measured directly for that same subset, at that subset's own n, 30 disjoint-halves trials) is reported alongside every number specifically so this cannot be misread as a quality difference. Only R-Precision is decisive for the spatial-vs-non-spatial comparison this experiment exists to make.

published_reproduction.note: MDM published Guo R-Precision-top3 (LANDSCAPE.md line 47, paper own table)
published_reproduction.interpretation: This project harness reproduces the published figure to within ordinary sampling noise, on the same released checkpoint, without training. See docs/EXPERIMENT_DESIGN_E3.md section 9.6 and docs/DECISIONS.md D-03.

published_fid_comparison.note: MDM published Guo FID, generated-vs-real (LANDSCAPE.md line 47, paper own table, 20-replication protocol)
published_fid_comparison.bootstrap_point_estimate_note: differs from measured_value_e3_record by 0.0020 (~0.4% relative), a small residual not further investigated -- both computed from the same cached motions, likely floating-point ordering sensitivity in the covariance/Frechet-distance computation, not a data or protocol discrepancy
published_fid_comparison.interpretation: Not distinguishable from the published figure under an uncertainty this test cannot tighten (accepted interval [0.335, 0.637], a +-15.5% window around the point estimate, vs R-Precision +-1.2%). This is a non-rejection, not a tight reproduction -- the two halves of D-03 are not the same strength of evidence; lead with R-Precision wherever both are cited. The bootstrap mean (0.5375) is biased upward by resampling-with-replacement (duplicated motions shrink effective diversity) and is NOT used as the estimate; the point estimate (0.4858) plus twice the bootstrap std is used instead to size the accepted interval. What would actually tighten this: independent regenerations with different sampled noise, the quantity the paper own 20-replication CI actually measures -- 3 total replications (2 more beyond this one) would cost ~8.1h of additional MPS compute at the measured 4.03h/run (artifacts/e3/generate.log) and yield a genuine between-replication spread; the full 20-replication protocol would need 19 more runs beyond this one, ~76.6h of additional MPS compute (~80.6h total across all 20, if counted from scratch). Both priced as the next candidate experiment for this gate, not undertaken -- the author own call whether either is worth spending. See docs/EXPERIMENT_DESIGN_E3.md section 9.7 and docs/DECISIONS.md D-03.
published_fid_comparison.verdict: non-rejection achieved, tight reproduction not achieved
